findings.message: The lead decision sentence ('Persist link records in a single durable, transactional key-value store keyed by short code.') is a clean single-sentence imperative and satisfies C1, but it is immediately followed by four further imperative sentences (atomic conditional write, durable-commit-before-acknowledge, primary-key read, off-path increment) in the same paragraph. These are sound and in-scope but blur which clause is THE binding decision versus its consequent write semantics.
findings.recommendation: Keep the first imperative as the standalone bolded decision and demote the four elaborating imperatives to a 'Decision semantics' sub-list (the §3 'Decision semantics' block already does this for reversibility/idempotency/trust-boundary). Optional precision nicety; the decision is already implementer-bindable as written.

findings.message: §2 scopes this ADR to 'only the storage substrate and its write semantics — not the cache, code generator, or replication model.' The per-service-principal auth/TLS decision (1050) and provider-managed envelope-encryption decision (0db1) are adjacent security postures bound here. They are legitimately store-coupled and well-bounded, so this is not P1/P2 scope creep, but a future reader could read them as decisions exceeding the stated 'storage substrate and write semantics' charter.
findings.recommendation: Add one clause to the §2 scope statement explicitly admitting the store's trust boundary and at-rest-encryption posture into scope (e.g. '...and the store's authentication and at-rest-encryption posture'), so the charter matches what §3/§6 actually decide. No decision change required.

notes: Re-audit it.2: prior C4 P2 (missing reversibility) is RESOLVED — §3 ADR.01.03.f5f5 now classifies one-way with rationale. C1-C5 all pass; 3 alternatives with concrete reject rationales; gains+gives-up explicit; KV-conditional-write assumption surfaced in §7 Phase-1 risk. Two P3 precision nits only.
